Before you buy anything that isn't a need, wait a day. Then write down what you'd charge a stranger for what you do, and charge that.

3.upright:
The third house is the near world. Messages and calls, siblings, neighbours, short drives and errands, the things you learn along the way. It's cadent, about processing and adjusting. There's a nice detail here for this card. The Moon has its joy in the third house, and the Moon rules Cancer, so the Chariot's own planet is happy in this territory, even though Cancer and Gemini, the house's natural sign, are neighbours with little in common. Water and air are neutral, so feeling and quick talk need introducing.

What you'll notice is that your words carry more feeling than usual. You say less and mean more of it, and you're harder to talk out of something once you've decided. Material you care about sticks, and the purely abstract stuff slides off. Mercury rules this house and likes speed, and the Chariot slows it to the pace of what you actually feel, which can be frustrating in a quick-fire group chat and very useful in a hard conversation.

With a brother or sister there's loyalty running under the ordinary bickering, and maybe a conversation about a parent you've both been circling. With neighbours it's small protective acts, the parcel taken in, the bin brought back. With study, the course that connects to something you'd defend is the one you'll finish. When a conversation matters, say the feeling in plain words, and stick to your point when the other person pulls.
3.reversed:
The third house reversed is where the Chariot's feeling gets into your words the wrong way. You say the sharp thing while hurt and regret the tone for days, or you go quiet and let messages sit because answering feels like too much. The Moon's joy in this house turns into moodiness, and short, ordinary exchanges carry a weight they shouldn't.

It shows in a sibling you're not speaking to over something small, in a group chat you've muted, in the drive where you rehearse the argument out loud. With neighbours it can be a minor dispute about a fence or the parking that somehow keeps growing. Before you send anything while upset, leave it in drafts for an hour. Then send the shorter version.

4.upright:
This is the Chariot's own house. The fourth is home, family and roots, the private ground nobody else sees, and its natural sign is Cancer, ruled by the Moon, so the card isn't visiting here. It lives here. The house is angular, one of the chart's corners, which makes home life decisive for everything else, and it's water meeting water, so the card speaks the house's language at full volume, for better and sometimes for too much.

What's live is how much the rest of your life leans on this part of it. When home is solid you can handle almost anything out there, and when it's shaky nothing feels right, however well the job's going. You may feel a pull to put down roots and make the place properly yours, or to finally sort out something in the family that's been sitting there for years. The Moon rules this house and the card, so moods move through the household quickly, and yours set the tone. The risk with this much water is going into home so completely that it turns into somewhere to hide.

With the house itself, put the effort into whatever would make it feel safe, the lock that sticks, the room nobody uses. With parents, old loyalties and old hurts may come up to be looked at, or a parent may need you to do some steering for them. With the people you live with, you're likely the one holding the place together. Spend a weekend on the one thing at home that unsettles you every time you walk past it.
4.reversed:
Upside down in its own house, the Chariot shakes the base. Something at home, a family tension, a living arrangement that's gone sour, a parent's needs, is doing the steering, and the place that ought to steady you is what's throwing you off course. Because this is the card's own ground, the trouble goes straight to the foundations. Sometimes it's the opposite, and you're clinging to a house or a family role long after it stopped holding you up.

It shows in a household where nobody quite says what's wrong, and in family visits that take days to recover from. It shows in restlessness about where you live, or in not being able to leave. Pick the one family conversation you've been putting off and have it, calmly, in person if you can. Then give yourself a quiet evening afterwards.

5.upright:
The fifth house is what you do for the fun of it. Romance, creativity, children, games, the hobby nobody pays you for. Its natural sign is Leo, fixed fire, ruled by the Sun, and Venus has her joy here, which makes it the chart's most openly pleasurable corner. The Chariot is Cancer's card, and Cancer sits right next to Leo with very little in common, the semi-sextile. Water in fire's house as well. So a card that holds things close has landed in the part of the chart that wants to show off.

That tension is what you'll feel. Delight has gone protective. You may be making something you care about too much to share yet, or falling for someone and wanting to keep it quiet and safe for a while before anyone else gets a say. Love goes deep quickly and wants somewhere to come home to. With children, yours or other people's, there's a fierce, proud tenderness. None of that is a problem, though the fifth house does want the fun let out eventually. It's succedent, a house where pleasure builds up over time if you let it.

In romance, commitment may arrive earlier than you expected. Creative work carries real feeling and needs handling kindly, by you as much as anyone. With kids it's the sports day or the school play where you're the loudest one watching. Let one thing you've made or loved be seen by someone who'll be kind about it, even though showing it feels exposed.
5.reversed:
In the fifth house reversed, fun is the thing that gets dropped. The Chariot's protectiveness turns against play, so the creative project goes back in the drawer the moment it might be judged, and romance swings between clinging and going cold. Or the drive takes over and hobbies become one more thing to win at, the fun run you train for like a job. Venus has her joy in this house and barely gets a look in.

It shows in weekends that are all errands, and in a relationship that's become about managing moods. With children it can look like worrying so much about them that you forget to enjoy them. Book one thing purely for pleasure, with nothing to achieve at the end of it, and keep the booking.

6.upright:
Keeping yourself going day to day is the sixth house's business. The routine, the job you actually do each day, the body's upkeep, meals, sleep, the dishes. It's cadent, about adjusting and serving. The Chariot fits better than you might think. Virgo is the house's natural sign, and Cancer sextiles Virgo, a cooperative link, water and earth getting on, feeling and practical care helping each other along. Mars has its joy in the sixth, which gives the daily round some drive.

What you'll notice is how closely your energy follows your feelings. When you're settled underneath, you can keep a routine going for months without much effort. When something's churning, the plan falls apart within days, however good it was. Stress goes straight to your stomach and your sleep with this card, and I'd treat that as information. The Chariot's steadiness works best here in small repeated things, the same walk, the same breakfast, the same bedtime, done most days.

At work you may be doing the caretaking nobody logs, checking in on people, the quiet upkeep that keeps a place running. In the body it's a good placement for building a routine you'll actually keep. With food it's eating at proper times and noticing what you reach for when you're upset. Choose one small daily thing that settles you, and do it at the same time every day for the next few weeks.
6.reversed:
Routines come apart, or get gripped so hard they hurt, when the card is reversed in the sixth house. The Chariot's drive turns into pushing the body past what it wants to do, and the feeling underneath gets ignored until it turns up as tension. Or the days lose their shape altogether, meals skipped, sleep all over the place, nothing done at a regular time.

It shows in the gut, the jaw, the lower back. At work it's doing everyone's upkeep and none of your own, staying late to cover for someone who didn't ask. Work out what feeling's been driving the overwork and name it, to yourself at least. Then put one fixed, gentle thing back into the day, like eating lunch sitting down.

7.upright:
The seventh house is the person opposite you. A partner, a business partner, anyone you've made a serious one-to-one agreement with. It's angular, so what happens here matters and doesn't stay quiet. Libra is its natural sign, Venus its ruler, and Cancer squares Libra from three signs away, both cardinal, both wanting to lead. Water and air have no special bond either way. So the Chariot brings a protective, feeling-led way of relating into a house built on fairness and balance, and the square makes the two rub.

The two sphinxes facing different ways in the picture are the easiest way to see it. There are two of you and two sets of instincts, and the card's question is whether you can agree where you're going and both keep a hand on it. You may be the one holding things together, getting the relationship through a rough patch on sheer commitment. It's a placement where loyalty gets tested and usually holds. The square means you'll keep having to renegotiate the line between being close and keeping your own course.

With a partner it could be a stretch of real teamwork on something hard, a move, a family illness, money. In business it's a partnership that needs clear terms, written down. With contracts, read them properly, because your sense of safety rides on the other person keeping their word. Sit down with your partner and agree, out loud, what the two of you are working toward.
7.reversed:
The seventh house with the Chariot reversed is a relationship with two drivers and no agreed direction. One of you pushes, the other digs in, and it turns into a contest of wills over things that shouldn't matter much, whose parents you visit, whose job gets to move. Or one of you has quietly stopped steering and is just being carried along.

It shows in arguments that repeat word for word, and in a business partner you've stopped trusting with the details. It shows in contracts signed in a hurry and resented later. Ask your partner what they think the two of you are heading toward, listen to the whole answer, and then give yours. Then talk about the parts that don't match.

8.upright:
Shared money, debt, inheritance, intimacy including sex, and the endings that change a life all belong to the eighth house. The house's natural sign is Scorpio, and Cancer trines Scorpio, four signs apart, both water. That's natural ease and the element doubled, so the card goes deep here without much resistance. It's succedent, about what builds up between people over time.

What the Chariot brings here is steadiness in the heavy stuff. You can go a long way into something with another person, a joint account, a mortgage, real closeness, a grief, and not lose yourself in it. That's a real strength. The risk with this much water is gripping too hard, holding onto a person or an arrangement past its time because letting go feels like drowning. Mars rules Scorpio in the old system, so there's some fight in this house, and the card tends to turn it into loyalty.

Joint money is the obvious place to use it, getting the arrangements properly sorted, who owns what and what happens if. In intimacy, trust grows slowly and runs deep, and closeness needs to feel safe before it opens up. With an ending, the card helps you get through it steadily, as long as you let it end. Book an hour with the person you share money with and go through the what-ifs, the will, the insurance, what happens to the house.
8.reversed:
In the eighth house the reversed Chariot's grip goes into control. Shared money becomes a quiet power struggle over who holds the account and who has to ask. Intimacy gets guarded, closeness offered and then taken back, and something that has ended keeps being held onto because the loss feels too big. Or the break is forced, made too hard and too fast so you don't have to feel it.

It shows in a joint account nobody's allowed to look at, in a debt that's been kept quiet, in an ex you still check up on. It can show in sex that's become about reassurance. Say the fear under the grip out loud, even if only to yourself. Then loosen one thing, a password shared, a question asked, a box finally cleared out.

9.upright:
The ninth house is the long view. Belief, study, travel, distance, the big questions about what your life is for. It's cadent, about learning and processing, and the Sun has its joy here. Sagittarius is its natural sign, and Cancer sits five signs from it, a quincunx, two signs with nothing in common that have to keep adjusting. Water in fire's house as well. So a homeward, protective card has landed in the most outward-looking part of the chart.

What that feels like is wanting to go far and needing to know where home is while you do. You may be drawn to study or travel with a personal thread through it, the family's old country, a course that connects to something you care about, a trip taken to see someone in particular. Beliefs you've held quietly may start to feel solid enough to say out loud. The quincunx means some awkwardness along the way, packing and unpacking, a plan changed twice.

With study, pick the one that means something to you personally, because that's the one that'll hold. With travel, the good trips have someone at the other end. With belief, you may find yourself defending something you used to keep to yourself, and doing it calmly. Plan one trip or course around a person or a place that matters to you, and book the first part of it.
9.reversed:
In the ninth house reversed, the far horizon and home pull you in half. You stay put when you wanted to go, the course never started, the trip postponed again. Or you bolt somewhere far away and find you've brought the unsettled feeling with you, and spend the trip on your phone to home. The quincunx keeps you adjusting the plan without ever moving on it.

It shows in study started three times and finished once, in a belief that wobbles the moment someone questions it, in in-laws from another background you can't quite settle with. The big questions can stop feeling worth asking. Choose one bigger thing you've been putting off, write down the first practical step, and give it a date.

10.upright:
Career and reputation, the part of your life strangers can see, belong to the tenth house. It's angular, the highest point of the chart. Capricorn is its natural sign and Saturn its ruler, and Cancer sits directly opposite Capricorn, so the Chariot is looking at this house from the other end of the home and career axis. Water and earth are friendly, though, so the pull between the two ends can be balanced.

In practice your work life and your private life are asking to be lined up. You may be moving forward at work, a new role, more responsibility, people starting to rely on you, and the card wants that to rest on something solid at home. Bosses tend to trust the Chariot sort of person, the one who keeps going under pressure and looks after the team. The opposition is the old strain of this axis, the job taking the evening the family needed, or needs at home holding you back from a step up.

In your job it's a good placement for steady advancement, the kind built on being dependable. With your reputation it's being known as someone who looks after people. With the pull between home and career it's being honest about what each is costing the other. Before you take on anything new at work, look at what it'll cost at home, and decide with that in front of you.
10.reversed:
The tenth house reversed is ambition that's lost its reason. You're pushing for a promotion you're not sure you want, or grinding on in a role because stopping feels like failing, and the private life that was meant to be the point has worn thin. Or it goes the other way and home worries leak into work, so you're distracted and less reliable than usual. Saturn rules this house and can keep you climbing out of habit.

It shows in the job that takes every evening, in a boss who's noticed you're somewhere else in your head, in children or a partner who get the tired version of you. Write down why you wanted the job or the goal in the first place, in one sentence. If the sentence doesn't hold up, change the goal.

11.upright:
The eleventh house is your wider circle. Friends, groups, networks, the club or the online community, and the hopes you have for later on. It's succedent, and Jupiter has its joy here, which gives the house a generous feel. Aquarius is its natural sign, fixed air, and Cancer is five signs from Aquarius, a quincunx, nothing in common and constant small adjustments. Air and water don't naturally meet, so the card's closeness and the house's group-mindedness have to be introduced.

What you might feel is a wish to make a group feel like family. You bring care into friendships where the house tends to keep things light, and you'll usually hold a group together by caring about the actual people in it, remembering birthdays, noticing who's gone quiet. The tension is between the closeness you want and the many-at-once nature of a big circle. You may find yourself drifting toward two or three close friends and away from the wider crowd, and that's fine.

With friends you're the one who organises the dinner and checks on the person who didn't come. With a group or a cause you take on the welfare side, making sure new people get talked to. With your hopes, the ones that last tend to include people you love. Ring one friend you've drifted from and suggest something specific, a date and a place.
11.reversed:
You can end up on the edge of your own circle when the card's reversed in the eleventh house. The guard goes up in groups, so you hang back, feel unseen by people who'd have been glad to see you, and read the group chat without joining in. Or you take a group's direction as your own and chase hopes that were never really yours because everyone else wanted them. The quincunx makes it all feel slightly out of step, as if you missed a conversation everyone else was in.

It shows in invitations turned down and then regretted, in a friendship that's gone one-sided, in a committee job you took on and resent. Pick the one or two friendships that really matter and put your energy there. Let a few of the others be lighter.

12.upright:
Sleep and dreams, retreat, the unconscious, what you do alone and what you don't quite admit, all of that is twelfth-house ground. It's cadent, about letting go, and Saturn has its joy here, which gives the house a bit of quiet structure. Its natural sign is Pisces, which Cancer trines from four signs off, the two sharing their element. Natural ease, the element doubled, so the card sinks in here without resistance.

What that feels like is a lot of your direction being set in private. Decisions may arrive after a night's sleep, or on a long walk alone, fully formed. You'll probably want more time to yourself, and it'll do you good, the quiet evening, the drive with no radio on. Too much water here and you can go so far inward that you disappear from your own life for a while, and the people who love you start to wonder where you've gone.

With sleep, pay attention to the dreams, especially the ones that keep coming back. With rest, time alone is doing real work, so protect it. With what's hidden, there may be an old feeling moving around underneath that will want looking at sooner or later. Set aside one evening a week that's yours alone, and tell the people you live with it isn't about them.
12.reversed:
A mood steering you from somewhere you can't see is the usual shape of the twelfth house reversed. You're off and can't say why. Old feelings come up in the small hours with no clear cause, and the retreat that usually restores you tips into hiding, the phone off, the curtains shut, the days blurring together. Saturn has its joy in this house, and upside down its quiet structure turns into isolation.

It shows in sleep that doesn't rest you, in dreams that stay with you all day, in a low feeling you haven't mentioned to anyone. Tell one person plainly that you've been down, and let them keep you company for an afternoon. If it doesn't lift, ask for proper help.
